newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank says to maintain money policy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank says to maintain money policy.

text.p: Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong on Saturday said the central bank would maintain its longstanding "stable-to-loose" monetary policy and denied that recent mop-up measures were a signal of imminent tightening.
"The central bank's monetary policy will not change. It will continue to be stable-to-loose," governor Sheu Yuan-dong told reporters.
"We will wait until all the industries have fully recovered (from recent sluggishness) before contemplating an adjustment," Sheu said.
Analysts are concerned that a tightening of policy could jeopardise the island's economic recovery from a 1996 slump.
Many of them viewed the central bank's recent persistent issuance of negotiable certificates of deposit as an effort to curb the stock market rally.

But Sheu said that although the central bank had issued a total of T$47 billion negotiable certificates of deposit in April, T$45 billion of them already have matured and returned to the banking system.
"In reality only T$20 billion was lifted out of the market," Sheu said.
The central bank repeatedly has denied that its NCD issues were aimed at curbing the loose liquidity that analysts said had been fuelling a previous stock rally.

The stock market, which at one point had risen by 27 percent in 1997 alone, has lost more than 300 points or four percent since April 28 on widespread concerns that many of the shares were overvalued.
